title: In 2 Chronicles 15 What Does It Mean To Seek The Lord With All Your Heart
paragraphs: Understanding 2 Chronicles 15: Seeking the Lord With All Your Heart

The phrase “seek the Lord with all your heart” is a central theme in 2 Chronicles 15. This chapter records a pivotal moment in the reign of King Asa of Judah, following a time of national distress, spiritual decline, and idolatry. Asa’s response to God’s message, delivered by the prophet Azariah, offers rich insight into what it truly means to seek the Lord wholeheartedly.
The Context of 2 Chronicles 15
After a period of relative peace, Asa faced the threat of enemies and the temptation of false gods. Into this context, “the Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded” who declared:

And he went out to meet Asa, and said unto him, Hear ye me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin: Jehovah is with you, while ye are with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you. - 2 Chronicles 15:2 ASV
The historian then describes Israel’s spiritual state:

Now for a long season Israel was without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law: but when in their distress they turned unto Jehovah, the God of Israel, and sought him, he was found of them. - 2 Chronicles 15:3-4 ASV
What Does It Mean to “Seek the Lord With All Your Heart”?
To “seek the Lord” means more than a casual interest or half-hearted effort. In the biblical sense, it implies:
Desiring God Above All: To seek God with all your heart is to place Him above every other pursuit or affection (Deuteronomy 6:5).

Turning From Sin: Asa led the people to remove idols and restore proper worship, showing that seeking God involves repentance and turning away from anything that competes with Him (2 Chronicles 15:8).

Obedience to God's Word: Asa “renewed the altar of Jehovah” and “gathered all Judah and Benjamin,” leading the people in covenant renewal. Seeking God is shown by aligning one’s life with His commands (2 Chronicles 15:12).
Wholehearted Commitment: The people “sought him with their whole desire; and he was found of them: and Jehovah gave them rest round about” (2 Chronicles 15:15).
New Testament Parallels
The call to seek the Lord wholeheartedly is echoed in the teachings of Jesus:
But seek ye first his kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. - Matthew 6:33 ASV
True seeking is not merely religious activity but flows from a transformed heart through faith in Christ. The promise is that God will be found by those who earnestly seek Him (Jeremiah 29:13).
Implications for Today
Seeking the Lord with all your heart means:
Pursuing a personal relationship with God through Jesus Christ (John 14:6).
Consistent repentance and turning from idols (anything that takes God’s rightful place).
Obeying God’s Word as the guide for life.
Engaging in worship, prayer, and community with other believers.
The assurance remains: if you seek God with all your heart, He will be found, and you will experience His presence, guidance, and peace.
Key Takeaways
Seeking God wholeheartedly is a call to undivided devotion.
It requires turning from sin and aligning life with God's Word.
God promises to draw near to those who earnestly seek Him.
